bread-wheat-or-cracked-wheat-with-raisin.title: Bread, wheat or cracked wheat, with raisins, toasted

content.title: About
content.content: Bread made from whole wheat or cracked wheat with raisins, toasted to a golden crust. It contains whole grains, natural sweetness from raisins, and the aroma of toasting. Suitable for breakfast, a snack, or as a base for sandwiches.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Toasting enhances flavor and creates a crunchy crust.
Raisins add natural sugars, making the bread slightly sweet without added sugar.
Whole wheat retains more fiber and nutrients compared with white bread.
Traditionally this bread is common in Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisines.
Toasted bread stays fresher longer than soft bread.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole grains and raisins provide dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat supplies thiamine, niacin, and folate, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Raisins are high in polyphenols, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports blood sugar balance
items.content: Fiber slows carbohydrate absorption, which can moderate glucose spikes.

items.title: Energy‑dense snack
items.content: The combination of complex carbs and natural sugars offers sustained satiety.

items.title: Wheat allergy / gluten sensitivity
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten intolerance may experience adverse reactions.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Raisins increase overall sugar levels, so diabetics should monitor portion size.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Toasted bread is more calorie‑dense than regular bread, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the bread plain, spread with butter, cheese, or nut butter, use in sandwiches, toast to desired crispness, or serve alongside soups and salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight container. For longer shelf life, keep refrigerated to prevent drying out and mold growth.

content.title: About
content.content: Light mayonnaise-type salad dressing is a creamy vinaigrette made from vegetable oils, egg yolks, vinegar and spices. It offers a smooth texture, mild flavor and considerably fewer calories than traditional mayonnaise.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The formula usually relies on rapeseed or sunflower oil, making it healthier than saturated‑fat‑rich versions.
Light versions often reduce the amount of egg or use egg substitutes, lowering cholesterol content.
Vinegar and lemon juice give the dressing its characteristic light tang.
Many flavor variations exist: herb, garlic, mustard, or spice‑infused versions.
It is a popular choice in diet‑focused meals and fast‑service restaurant menus.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: Compared with regular mayonnaise, the light dressing provides roughly two‑to‑three times fewer calories, helping with energy balance.

items.title: Rich in monounsaturated fats
items.content: The vegetable oils supply monounsaturated fatty acids that support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: The oils are a good source of vitamin E, an antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: May contain probiotics (in some formulations)
items.content: If fermented vinegar is used, the dressing can contribute to a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins
items.content: A small amount of fat aids the body in absorbing vitamins A, D, E and K from vegetables served with the dressing.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Traditional recipes contain egg yolks, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some brands add noticeable amounts of salt; people monitoring blood pressure should check the sodium level.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: To extend shelf life, preservatives may be used, which can be problematic for those with sensitivities to food additives.

items.title: Possible trans fats (rare)
items.content: If partially hydrogenated oil is present, trans fats may be included, which are detrimental to heart health.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: The dressing works well on salads, vegetable sticks, sandwiches and wraps. It can also serve as a base for marinades, grill sauces, or a light herb dip.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store refrigerated at 2 °C–5 °C. After opening, consume within 7‑10 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may separate.

content.title: About
content.content: Powerade is an isotonic sports drink designed to replenish electrolytes and energy lost during intense physical activity. It contains water, carbohydrates, sodium, potassium, and B‑vitamins, helping to maintain hydration and improve endurance.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Powerade was first launched in 2002 as a competitor to Gatorade.
The lineup includes several flavors such as Lemon‑Lime, Berry Mix, and Tropical Fruit.
Some versions are fortified with creatine or higher‑sodium electrolytes for extreme conditions.
The brand actively sponsors sports events and teams worldwide.

items.title: Electrolyte balance restoration
items.content: Sodium and potassium help quickly replace electrolytes lost through sweat, reducing the risk of cramps.

items.title: Energy support
items.content: Carbohydrates (typically 6‑10% solution) provide a rapid source of fuel for working muscles.

items.title: Improved hydration
items.content: The drink’s osmolality is optimized for fast absorption into the bloodstream, speeding up rehydration.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: B‑vitamins aid in converting carbohydrates into energy and support the nervous system.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some Powerade variants contain up to 6 g of sugar per 100 ml, which may be undesirable for low‑sugar diets.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: The drink may contain flavorings, colorants, and preservatives that can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Excess sodium
items.content: Consuming large amounts can lead to high sodium intake, which is not recommended for people with hypertension.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Drink Powerade 15‑30 minutes before exercise and/or within the first 30‑60 minutes of activity. For recovery after prolonged sessions, consume 500‑750 ml, divided into several sips.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, consume within 24 hours and keep the cap tightly sealed.
